newsitem.title: UK: UK petrol site closures double in 1996 to 1,496-IP.
newsitem.headline: UK petrol site closures double in 1996 to 1,496-IP.

text.p: The number of U.K. petrol sites that closed in 1996 reached 1,496, nearly double from the previous year and leaving the total number of filling stations at 14,478, the Institute of Petroleum said on Friday.

The sharp increase in the petrol site closures "provides proof of the difficulties caused by last year's petrol price war and the continuing struggle to make profits," the IP, an industry trade group, said.

Esso, a unit of U.S. oil giant Exxon Corp, was still the largest U.K. petrol supplier, with 1,980 sites, followed by Shell with 1,706 sites, down from 2,028 and 1,905 the previous year respectively, according to the IP.
But the supermarkets continued to grow and showed a 6.5 percent expansion last year, it said.
There were a total of 16,244 petrol sites at the end of 1995, which was down 727 from 16,971 at the end of 1994, according to IP figures.
IP said the figures were based on a survey at the end of 1996 and therefore does not reflect changes that have been announced or taken place since then.
